goal: Define the maximum safe and technically supported Android-to-Kodi automation flow after a second explicit owner consent, without bypassing operating-system or Kodi trust confirmations.
success_criteria: Map every current manual step from setup APK through Bootstrap activation and classify it as safely automatable, platform-confirmed, or prohibited.
Verify Android PackageInstaller, scoped-storage, Fire OS/Android 9, modern Android, Kodi add-on installation, and Kodi JSON-RPC constraints from source and primary documentation.
Specify the second-consent text, scope, persistence, revocation, resume behavior, failure recovery, telemetry boundary, and tests needed for implementation.
Reject arbitrary file/settings access, silent APK confirmation, remote shell/ADB, accessibility automation, database tampering, and consent that purports to override system confirmations.
primary_hypothesis: The app can safely automate verified download, export, platform launch, state detection, and resume around explicit confirmations, but cannot silently approve Android packages or Kodi's initial add-on trust boundary.
discriminating_check: For each manual step, identify the exact current enforcement API and determine whether an official bounded API exists that preserves visible user confirmation.
stop_conditions: The analysis requires a secret, sensitive full settings file, or device mutation.
Primary documentation cannot establish a material platform capability.
The requested behavior is possible only through shell, ADB, accessibility, root, or direct Kodi database manipulation.
